situation:
You are the financial analyst at HARVEST LANE WHOLESALE GROCERS, a grocery wholesaler that buys produce and dry goods by the truckload and delivers them to independent corner stores across the region. The chief executive (judge) started the company two years ago and has asked you to recommend how it should answer a supplier who wants to be paid sooner.

The company opened on a single round of outside funding, and that money is nearly spent. Its reputation with the independent grocers rests on one promise: the lowest case price in the region on staple produce. Wholesale margins have thinned across the industry as delivery apps pull volume away from corner stores, and the company's own payment records are the only current picture anyone has of that trend.

The produce supplier that provides most of that staple volume has asked to be paid in fifteen days instead of the forty-five days it agreed to at the start. Accepting the shorter payment terms keeps the low case price the company advertises, and it costs the company its cash cushion, because the corner stores still pay their own invoices in thirty days and payroll, fuel and truck leases come due first.

A second wholesaler will supply the same staples on the original forty-five-day terms at a higher price per case. Moving the produce volume to that second wholesaler protects the cash the company has left, and it costs the low case price the brand rests on, because the higher price would be passed to the corner stores, which is the one thing keeping them from ordering from a national distributor.

The chief executive (judge) has asked you to explain what financial-information management covers at a company this size, show how the payment records already on hand can be read for something other than billing, demonstrate the analysis behind your figures, explain what the low-price brand is worth, describe the trends shaping wholesale grocery, and recommend which supplier arrangement to take.

The chief executive (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the questions, the chief executive (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the chief executive (judge) of HARVEST LANE WHOLESALE GROCERS. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You started the company two years ago on a single round of outside funding, and that money is nearly spent. You want the financial analyst to explain what financial-information management covers at a company this size, show how the payment records already on hand can be read for something other than billing, demonstrate the analysis behind the figures, explain what the low-price brand is worth, describe the trends shaping wholesale grocery, and tell you plainly whether to accept the produce supplier's shorter payment terms or move the volume to the second wholesaler.

After the financial analyst has presented, you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: What would the other supplier arrangement have given us that this one does not?
If we had gone the other way, what would that have cost the company?
